afghanistan.title: Flag of Afghanistan

colors.note: Field of the current (post-2021) flag; bears the black Shahada inscription.
Shahada text; in the pre-2021 tricolour represented the dark past of foreign occupation.
In the pre-2021 tricolour, represents the blood shed for independence.
In the pre-2021 tricolour, symbolises Islam, hope, and prosperity.

desc:
- The current flag of the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan is a plain white field bearing the Shahada (Islamic declaration of faith) in black Arabic script
- It was adopted upon the Taliban's return to power on 15 August 2021
- The previous flag (2004–2021) of the Islamic Republic was a vertical tricolour of black, red, and green with the national emblem — a mosque, Shahada, and wheat sheaves — in white at the centre
- Afghanistan has had more flag changes than almost any other country — over 20 designs since 1901, reflecting its turbulent political history
- Construction (pre-2021 tricolour): three equal vertical bands of black (hoist), red, and green
- The national emblem is centred, spanning roughly half the flag's height
- Ratio 2:3
afghanistan.note: The tricolor of black-red-green (with national emblem) was used from 2004 to 2021 under the Islamic Republic.
trivia:
- Only country to have changed its flag more than 20 times since 1900, reflecting decades of political upheaval
- The Taliban's plain white flag is one of the simplest national flags ever used
- The black-red-green tricolour's colours represent the dark past (black), blood shed for independence (red), and hope/Islam (green)

af-kingdom.title: Flag of the Kingdom of Afghanistan

colors.note: Represents the dark past of colonial rule under the Kingdom.
Blood of those who fought for sovereignty.
Islam, prosperity, and the Afghan agricultural heartland.

desc:
- The flag of the Kingdom of Afghanistan (1929–1973) was a black, red, and green vertical tricolour with a white national emblem centred
- This design continued the tradition of the Afghan tricolour but with royal emblems reflecting the monarchy under King Mohammed Zahir Shah
- The kingdom was overthrown in a coup in 1973
- **Construction:** three equal vertical bands of black (hoist), red, and green, with the royal emblem centred on the red stripe. Ratio 2:3
trivia:
- Afghanistan's royal emblem on this flag reflected King Mohammed Zahir Shah's modernization efforts
- The kingdom lasted from 1929–1973, during Afghanistan's most stable modern period
- This design bridged traditional Afghan symbols with Western heraldic conventions

af-republic.title: Flag of the Republic of Afghanistan

colors.note: Heritage from the traditional Afghan tricolour.
Blood shed for independence and revolution.
Islam and hope for the future.

desc:
- The flag of the Republic of Afghanistan (1973–1978) used the same black-red-green vertical tricolour with a modified emblem omitting the royal crown
- After Mohammed Daoud Khan's republican coup in 1973, the monarchy was abolished and the flag's emblem was updated to reflect the new republic
- This flag was short-lived, replaced after the Saur Revolution in 1978
- **Construction:** three equal vertical bands of black (hoist), red, and green. The eagle-based republican emblem sits centred. Ratio 2:3
trivia:
- Adopted after Mohammed Daoud Khan's 1973 coup that abolished the 240-year monarchy
- Lasted only five years before the communist Saur Revolution replaced it in 1978
- The republican emblem omitted the royal crown, symbolising the end of monarchy

af-soviet.title: Flag of the Democratic Republic of Afghanistan

colors.note: Communist revolution and solidarity with the USSR.

desc:
- The flag of Soviet-era Afghanistan (1978–1992) evolved through several versions, most featuring a red field or red element reflecting the country's alignment with the Soviet Union during the Saur Revolution and subsequent communist rule
- Early versions were predominantly red; later versions reintroduced the tricolour with modified socialist emblems
- The final version (1987) returned to the traditional black-red-green but with a new state seal
- **Construction:** various designs; the most recognisable was a red field with the state seal in the canton. Ratio 2:3
trivia:
- Afghanistan was the Soviet Union's only direct invasion of a Muslim-majority country
- The flag evolved through 14 years of conflict, reflecting shifting communist leadership
- The final version reintroduced the traditional tricolour with a socialist seal, attempting to reconcile tradition and ideology

af-taliban-1996.title: Flag of the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan (1996)

colors.note: Purity and the Taliban's interpretation of Islamic governance.

desc:
- The flag used by the Taliban during their first rule (1996–2001) was a plain white field bearing the Shahada (Islamic declaration of faith) in black Arabic script
- This stark, minimalist design signalled the Taliban's austere interpretation of Islamic governance
- It was also used by the Islamic Emirate after 2021, making it the de facto national flag again
- **Construction:** a plain white field with the Shahada inscribed centrally in black Nastaliq script. Ratio 2:3
trivia:
- One of only two flags in the world that is a plain colour with only text (the other being Libya's old green flag)
- The Shahada (Islamic declaration of faith) is the world's most common phrase on national flags
- Used by the Taliban in both their 1996–2001 and 2021–present periods of rule

af-islamic-republic.title: Flag of the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan

colors.note: The dark past overcome by the nation.
Sacrifice in the struggle for independence.
Islam, prosperity, and the natural beauty of Afghanistan.

desc:
- The flag of the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan (2004–2021) was a black, red, and green vertical tricolour bearing a white national emblem — a mosque with mihrab, Shahada, and wheat sheaves — at the centre
- Adopted in January 2004 under the new constitution, it replaced the various mujahedin and Taliban-era flags
- The emblem included the year 1298 (1919 CE, when Afghanistan gained independence from British influence)
- **Construction:** three equal vertical bands of black (hoist), red, and green. The white emblem is centred on the red band. Ratio 2:3
trivia:
- The national emblem includes the year 1298 (Islamic calendar), corresponding to 1919 CE when Afghanistan gained independence from Britain
- This 17-year flag (2004–2021) represented Afghanistan's longest democratic period
- The wheat sheaves symbolized Afghanistan's agricultural heritage and rural identity
